title: Uncovering the lair of the 'Butcher of Bucha'
subhead: Russian Colonel Azatbek Omurbekov's men carried out massacres of Ukrainians in the Kyiv region in March 2022. Le Monde traced his presence to a school in a Ukrainian village near the capital, Andriivka, from where he gave his orders.

title: Controversy after mock election votes for neo-Nazis at school attended by Swedish Crown Princess’s children
subhead: In a mock election held at Campus Manilla as part of a civic education exercise, 4.7% of young students voted for the Nordic Resistance Movement, a neo-Nazi group. In response, school officials announced plans to strengthen lessons on democracy and human rights.

title: 'Minotaur,' France's Oscar pick: An unflinching portrait of a country's moral decay
subhead: France's Oscar committee on Wednesday chose Cannes Grand Prix winner 'Minotaur' to represent the country at the Academy Awards in 2027. Shot by Russian director Andrey Zvyagintsev in Latvia, the film aligns its aesthetics with the moral darkness it portrays.

title: 'For the US authorities, the Taliban are reliable partners'
subhead: Political scientist Olivier Roy explains why, a quarter of a century after the 2001 terrorist attacks, the US has no choice but to normalize its relations with the Taliban, who, at the time, protected Al-Qaeda and harbored it in Afghanistan.

subhead: 'The Putin System' (1/3). The many 'siloviki,' officers drawn from Russia's security services, have seized power and are now omnipresent among the country's elites. Within society, they have spread an atmosphere of fear and suspicion that prohibits any questioning of the Kremlin or its war in Ukraine.

title: Mass surveillance and self-sufficiency: How China's leadership is reviving Mao's old principles
subhead: 'Mao's Fraught Legacy' (5/7). In 1963, Mao Zedong made the village of Fengqiao an example of how to encourage mass mobilization and resolve conflicts locally. Under Xi Jinping, the experiment has evolved into a system ensuring Beijing's absolute control.

title: Vast Gallic coin workshop discovered in central France
subhead: Excavations carried out this summer at the Arverni site of Corent in central France have revealed a building where gold and silver coins may have been minted before the Roman conquest of Gaul.
